subject: computer-science
title: Interrupts, Polling and Deadlocks
welcome_lead: Handle events efficiently and beware the four conditions of deadlock.
meta_desc: CS adventure on interrupts, polling and the four Coffman deadlock conditions.
final_note: Break any Coffman condition to prevent deadlock!

concepts.def: Interrupt Service Routine handles the event.
Processes stuck waiting on each other.
Process never gets the resource it needs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Interrupt: event-driven, low CPU overhead.

Polling: simple but wastes CPU on idle checks.

P1 holds R1, waits R2; P2 holds R2, waits R1.

All four Coffman conditions met - classic deadlock.

Order resources globally; processes request in fixed order.

Breaks circular wait - deadlock can't form.
